chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The one in a state of major impurity (Janub), whatever water flows upon his body, be it little or a lot, has sufficed him.

key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The one in a state of major ritual impurity, typically after sexual intercourse or ejaculation.
key_terms.قَلِيلُهُ وَ كَثِيرُهُ: Its little and its much (little or a lot).

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of water required for Ghusl (ritual bath) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the minimal requirement for Ghusl al-Janab, emphasizing that the sufficiency of water is determined by its flow over the body rather than a fixed volume. This ruling supports the Shia view of 'Qalil al-Ma'' (small quantity water) purity, distinguishing it from the Hanafi reliance on 'Kathir al-Ma'' (sea water) for major impurity. It underscores the principle that ritual purity is achieved through the physical act of water reaching the skin, aligning with the Quranic command to purify oneself.
